Lemma
[completeness forces a covering map]

Source: petersen:page-0214 ↗ def:pet-ch5-local-isometry ↗ def:pet-ch5-geodesically-complete ↗ cor:pet-ch5-uniform-injectivity-radius-compact 1. ch5:5.6.4If $F:(M,g_M)\to (N,g_N)$ is a local Riemannian isometry, $M$ geodesically complete, $N$ connected, then $F$ is a Riemannian covering map.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch5-local-isometry-covering ↗ prop:pet-ch5-local-isometry-properties \sketch Choose $\varepsilon $ with $\exp _q:B(0,\varepsilon )\to B(q,\varepsilon )$ a diffeomorphism. Completeness defines the corresponding exponentials at each $p\in F^{-1}(q)$, and subsection 6.1 gives $F\circ \exp _p(v)=\exp _q(DF_p(v))$ for $v\in B(0,\varepsilon )$; as $\exp _q$ and Hence $F:B(p,\varepsilon )\to B(q,\varepsilon )$ is a diffeomorphism.

Conversely, lift the unique radial segment from $q$ to $F(x)$ backwards from $x$. Completeness and section 2 put $x$ in a unique such ball, so these balls evenly cover $F^{-1}(B(q,\varepsilon ))$.

The image is open. It is closed because item 2 gives one radius for a convergent image sequence and its limit. Connectedness of $N$ gives surjectivity.

□
